England is transcribed from the National Archives snapshot of 6 September 2024 of the GOV.UK page, under the heading 'Weekly allowances for the tax year from 6 April 2024 to 5 April 2025', as published at the time and NOT back-calculated from the 6.88% uplift. That page states 'This guidance applies to England'. Scotland was added on 31 August 2026: the Scottish Recommended Allowance was not uprated for 2024/25, so the rates introduced on 29 August 2023 stood for the whole year. Wales and Northern Ireland stay null, so backdating blocks 2024/25 for those two nations rather than guessing. Cross-check for England: applying the announced 3.55% uplift to every one of these 15 cells reproduces the 2025/26 table within a pound, and the range 165 to 289 pounds matches the endpoints reported independently in secondary sources.

scotland.note: The Scottish Recommended Allowance was NOT uprated for 2024/25. The rates announced on 29 August 2023 remained in force for the whole financial year, which is why upliftPercent is 0 rather than absent. Scotland publishes four bands (0-4, 5-10, 11-15, 16+) but pays 5-10 and 11-15 the same, which is the three-band design the SRA is built on and the shape this table uses. gov.scot's own August 2023 release gives 11-15 as 19581, identical to 5-10. Several local authority reproductions of the same table instead show 20251 for 11-15. The primary source wins, so 19581 is what ships. The other bands agree across both. Do not switch to 20251 without a gov.scot page or an archived capture saying so.
